title: Walk 17: put a project on a host and take it off again

steps.say: Start the two mock daemons and the interface with the host stand-ins as described in the guided walk. Create the walk folder and invented keys first: mkdir -p /tmp/porelo-walk/keys /tmp/porelo-walk/tresor && ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C walk-invented -f /tmp/porelo-walk/keys/walk_ed25519. Use only invented answers in this walk.
Open Projects in the rail, choose checkout, then its menu and Put this project on a server…. The title names the project and the first step is Where it is rented.

Give the Scaleway project id walk and keep account porelo. Read where the id is found in the Scaleway console and which saved provider key is used. Next stays unavailable until the step is complete. Click Next.

The drive is Tresorit. Choose /tmp/porelo-walk/tresor as Its synced folder on this computer. Its path appears beside Choose…, and The tresor's name in Tresorit fills with tresor. Change that name to walk; the server syncs by this name, while the folder holds this computer's copy. The repository address and signing-key fields appear.

Give repository address https://example.org/walk.git and signing key /tmp/porelo-walk/keys/walk_ed25519.pub. Each path field has Choose… beside it. Click Back and check the project id and account stayed; click Next to return and check the drive answers stayed. Then click Next to Your ssh keys.

The private ssh key comes first. Type /tmp/porelo-walk/keys/walk_ed25519.pub there: it is refused as a public key, and Next cannot run. Try ~nobody/key: only ~/ is understood, so it is also refused before any host starts. Give /tmp/porelo-walk/keys/walk_ed25519 as the private key and /tmp/porelo-walk/keys/walk_ed25519.pub as the public one. Each has its own Choose…. Click Next.
Choose /tmp/porelo-walk/porelo-host as the server setup file. Click Next. Check and start shows the values from every step. Nothing has been rented yet.

Read every answer, then click Put it on a server. The action step shows its progress and reaches a stop asking for the drive and a new vault. Back and Leave ask before leaving unfinished work; choose Stay to keep watching it.
Enter an invented plain Tresorit e-mail address. There must be no password, code or passphrase field in this dialog.

Click Open a terminal on the host. Read the warning about the visible one-time code. Type an invented password, then an invented one-time code, then a vault passphrase twice into the terminal prompts. Each command says what completed and what comes next.
When the terminal ends, click Done. Host setup runs up again without answers. The steps finish and the completed host can be added.
Hover the (i) beside Save the VPN connection to this server. It says what WireGuard is, that the file holds a private key and where to keep it, and the two commands that bring the VPN up.
Click Add this server to your machines, then Finish. Open Machines and checkout server. It should answer through the second mock daemon, with only checkout and no work run yet.
Open Projects in the rail, choose checkout on the host, then its menu and Put this project on a server…. Give the same project id and account in Where it is rented, then Next.

Give the same tresor, repository and signing key; the local folder is remembered. Next opens Your ssh keys. Keep the same keys and click Next. Give the same setup file and click Next to Check and start.
Click Take it off the server. The give-back step finishes with Done. Click Finish and check Machines: checkout server has been removed; the first mock machine remains.
Finish the wizard and record anything that differed. To try a refusal or a slow step, change the situation in host-standin.json and reopen the dialog.
